title: Compatible coefficient fields and a source Cohen presentation
statement:
Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m,K)\to(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be a local homomorphism of nonzero commutative Noetherian local $\mathbf Q$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means $f(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, $K=A/\mathfrak m$, $L=B/\mathfrak n$, and $\iota:K\hookrightarrow L$ is the induced field inclusion. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are complete for their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. There exist residue-field sections $a:K\to A$ and $b:L\to B$, an integer $e\geq0$, elements $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$, and a continuous surjective local homomorphism $q:R=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that
$$b\circ\iota=f\circ a,\qquad q(c)=a(c)\ (c\in K),\qquad q(X_i)=x_i.$$
Writing $\mathfrak r=(X_1,\ldots,X_e)R$ and $I=\ker q$, one has $I\subseteq\mathfrak r$, and the induced map $R/I\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ is an isomorphism of complete local $K$-algebras for the structure given by $a$. No flatness, regularity, or finite type hypothesis on $f$ or on $L/K$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated compatible-section and source-presentation input: Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), characteristic-zero coefficient-field construction and final proof paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous) applied to the unrestricted residue extension. Extracted from original steps 3--4 of lem-trf-relative-cohen-flat-presentation; compatibility is a refinement, not quoted verbatim from 032A.

proof.text: Write $\rho_A:A\to K$ and $\rho_B:B\to L$ for the residue maps. The nonzero $\mathbf Q$-algebra $K$ has characteristic zero. Apply the residue-section theorem to $A$ to choose $a:K\to A$ with $\rho_Aa=1_K$. Then $h=fa:K\to B$ satisfies $\rho_Bh=\iota$, so it makes $B$ a $K$-algebra and its residue algebra is $L$ with structure map $\iota$.

The extension $L/K$ is formally smooth, since $K$ has characteristic zero; there is no algebraicity or finite-generation restriction. Apply the complete-target lifting theorem with base $K$, source $L$, source ideal $0$, target $B$, ideals $I=J=\mathfrak n$, $t=r=1$, and residue map $g=1_L:L\to B/\mathfrak n$. Here $J^t\subseteq I$ and $\bigcap_{s\ge1}(J+I^s)=\mathfrak n=J$; $g(0)=0$. The target is $I$-adically complete by hypothesis. Thus there is a $K$-algebra map $b:L\to B$ with $\rho_Bb=1_L$. Its $K$-linearity gives $b\iota=h=fa$.

Noetherianity makes $\mathfrak m$ finitely generated; choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_e$, allowing $e=0$. Apply the fixed-section generator-presentation theorem with field $K$, target $A$, residue identification $1_K$ and section $a$. It gives a continuous surjective $K$-algebra map $q:K[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]\to A$, restricting to $a$ on constants and sending $X_i$ to $x_i$, with $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Tag 0C52, lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra, final paragraph, with Algebra Tag 0315

proof.text: The power-series local-ring theorem over $K$ makes $R$ local. Every variable has zero constant term, so $\mathfrak r$ is contained in its maximal ideal. Conversely any $F$ outside $\mathfrak r=q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$ has $q(F)$ a unit of $A$. To identify the maximal ideal without assuming units lift, note that a series $F$ with zero constant term lies in $(X_1,\ldots,X_e)$: assign each nonconstant monomial to its first variable with positive exponent, obtaining $F=\sum_iX_iF_i$. Thus the maximal ideal is exactly $\mathfrak r$, so $q$ is local. Also $I=\ker q\subseteq q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Tag 032A, theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, final paragraph; power-series unit criterion

proof.text: Put $I=\ker q$. The map $\bar q:R/I\to A$, $[F]\mapsto q(F)$, is well-defined and injective by the definition of $I$, and surjective because $q$ is. It is a $K$-algebra isomorphism since $q(c)=a(c)$. Moreover $q(\mathfrak r^s)=\mathfrak m^s$: both sides are generated by products of $s$ chosen generators and $q$ is surjective. Thus $\bar q$ identifies $(\mathfrak r/I)^s$ with $\mathfrak m^s$ for every $s$, making both directions continuous and identifying all adic quotients. Completeness of $A$ therefore gives completeness of $R/I$; its unique maximal ideal is $\mathfrak r/I$. This proves the asserted isomorphism of complete local $K$-algebras.
